about: BD-1047 (docs/187 B and G): written targets for the designed food map (src/shared/FoodLayerData.luau). tools/verify_food_layer.py fails when the map breaks one. PROVISIONAL numbers, measured on the committed map with tools/layer_stats.py (256-cell grid: blocks of 10 / 20 / 30 cells = 32 / 65 / 97 studs) and tools/food_pace.py (a rough walker model, NOT a real player), kept a little loose on purpose.

clusters.about: Foods are small clusters of 3 to 5 about 3 to 3.5 studs apart (like today's bundles of 9, only smaller). Groups are found by linking foods closer than link_distance; the 2 starter patches (9 foods) and the 4 lone ambers on the mountain tops are the only other groups.

obstacles.about: BD-1098 (docs/187 G): no food closer than margin studs to a solid world prop (rock, trunk, log, landmark, arch pillar, boundary boulder; tools/world_colliders.py). FoodService rejects a spot when a 1.25 stud ray hits a collider and the Studio check counted a food inside a box when its part touched it (up to 0.87 stud from the middle), so 1.5 clears both.

pace.about: Rough 5-minute walker model (tools/food_pace.py) on the map divided by the same model on today's placement (mean of 6 layouts, tools/dump_food_layout.py). The handbook says food pace stays about the same; the 'just runs around' walker matches the 600 to 700 food of a real 5-minute run, the two seeking walkers are far above it (idealised).
